full_sentence: Having reviewed the evidence carefully, the committee issued a cautious statement.
acceptable_variants: the committee then published a measured response.
the committee chose to make a careful announcement.

options.text: the evidence was reviewed by the committee.
options.why_wrong: The participle clause 'Having reviewed the evidence' needs the main subject as its doer. Here the evidence would be the one reviewing, which is illogical.

options.text: the committee issued a cautious statement.
the statement was reviewed by the committee.
options.why_wrong: A statement cannot review evidence, so the subject of the participle clause does not match the main clause.
This is an infinitive fragment with no finite verb after the comma, so it cannot complete the sentence as a main clause.

grammar_focus: Participle clauses with a matching subject
explanation: A participle clause at the start of a sentence describes an action completed before the main action. Its implied subject must be the same as the subject of the main clause, which is the committee in this case.
